newsitem.title: AZERBAIJAN: Azerbaijan police deny anti-communist crackdown.
newsitem.headline: Azerbaijan police deny anti-communist crackdown.

text.p: Azeri police officials said on Monday one of the republic's small communist parties had held an unlawful congress over the weekend but denied allegations by party members that they had broken it up.
Journalists said men in plain clothes entered a hall where around 300 members of the Azerbaijan Communist Party were meeting on Sunday and began beating several participants with their fists.
Party officials said they were policemen and that party leader, Ramiz Akhmedov, had been detained by police officials.

Etibar Kazibekov, police chief in Baku's Surakhani region, denied that authorities had anything to do with breaking up the meeting. He said Akhmedov had been "invited for a conversation with police officials" and had subsequently left.

Opposition politicians and parties often complain of harassment by the government of President Haydar Aliyev, which human rights groups say has censored the press, arrested detractors and keeps a tight reign over the former Soviet republic of eight million.
The Azerbaijan Communist Party was not allowed by the government to participate in the country's last parliamentary vote in 1995.
Kazibekov said the party had obtained permission to hold the congress on Monday but had violated the law by deciding to hold it a day earlier.

"The Mayor had been approached by the party about having a congress on Monday, but they tried to have it a day earlier. Therefore the congress was unlawful and there was no permission to hold it. We explained to Mr. Akhmedov that it was forbidden to carry on the congress," he told Reuters.
Akhmedov did not answer his telephone on Monday and efforts to contact members of the party for comment were unsuccessful.
